issues.legal_issue: Lessee liability for rent is joint and several when the lease creates a joint rent obligation despite allocating shares among the lessees.
material_facts: The lease stated an annual rent for the leased forest rights and allocated shares of the lessees’ interests and rent contributions.
The lease provided that the entire lease could be terminated if rent remained unpaid for two consecutive years.

The plaintiffs sued to recover their share of rent from the lessees and a transferee of part of a lessee’s interest; the transferee’s liability was treated as standing on the same footing as the lessees’.
issues.conclusion: The defendants were jointly and severally liable for the plaintiffs’ share of rent for the years not barred by limitation.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 43 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, persons who jointly promise to perform an obligation are, absent a contrary agreement, jointly and severally liable. The lease’s allocation of shares indicated contributions toward rent jointly payable; the provision making the entire lease terminable for rent default showed the joint nature of the obligation.

rule.if: rent_recovery_proceeding and lease_creates_joint_rent_obligation and lease_allocates_contribution_shares and entire_lease_subject_to_termination_for_rent_default

predicates.rent_recovery_proceeding: A claimant brought a proceeding to recover rent due under a lease.
predicates.lease_creates_joint_rent_obligation: The lease makes the lessees collectively responsible for paying the rent.
predicates.lease_allocates_contribution_shares: The lease specifies the lessees’ shares to indicate their respective contributions toward the rent.
predicates.entire_lease_subject_to_termination_for_: The lease makes the whole lease liable to termination if rent is left unpaid for the specified consecutive period.

issues.definition: When a rent-recovery proceeding concerns a lease that creates a collective rent obligation, allocates contribution shares, and subjects the whole lease to termination for rent default, the lessees are jointly and severally liable for the rent.

issues.legal_issue: A limitation defense may be considered even when it was not pleaded in the written statement if the governing law requires dismissal of a suit filed after limitation expires.
material_facts: The defendants did not plead limitation in their written statement.
The suit included claims for rent that the court found were filed after the applicable limitation period had expired.
The court found that the appellants could identify no further evidence they could have adduced on limitation and that the absence of the plea caused no prejudice.
issues.conclusion: The defendants were properly allowed to raise the limitation point despite not pleading it in the written statement.
issues.legal_principle: Section 184 of the Bihar Tenancy Act, 1885 requires dismissal of a suit instituted after limitation has expired even if limitation has not been pleaded. The court also relied on the absence of prejudice from allowing the point to be raised.

rule.if: tenancy_suit and limitation_not_pleaded and limitation_period_expired and law_requires_dismissal_after_expiry and no_prejudice_from_late_plea

predicates.tenancy_suit: A claimant brought a suit governed by the tenancy-law limitation regime.
predicates.limitation_not_pleaded: The defendant did not raise limitation in the written statement.
predicates.limitation_period_expired: The suit was instituted after the applicable limitation period had expired.
predicates.law_requires_dismissal_after_expiry: The governing law requires dismissal of a suit filed after limitation expires even if limitation was not pleaded.
predicates.no_prejudice_from_late_plea: The party opposing consideration of limitation could identify no further evidence it would have adduced and suffered no prejudice from the point being raised.

issues.definition: If a tenancy suit was filed after limitation expired, the governing law requires dismissal despite the absence of a pleaded limitation defense, and considering the defense causes no prejudice, the defense may be considered without pleading.

issues.legal_issue: A claim for rent for the enjoyment of forest produce is governed by the special limitation period for that subject even when the claim is founded on a registered instrument.
material_facts: The lease gave the lessees rights to cut and appropriate specified trees and to take the fruits and flowers of specified fruit-bearing trees.
Rights to open roads and construct buildings were incidental to enjoying the forest produce.
The plaintiffs sued to recover rent in respect of the forest produce, and the claims for two of the Fasli years were outside the applicable special limitation period.
The rent claim was founded on a registered lease instrument.
issues.conclusion: The suit was governed by Article 2(b)(i) of Schedule III to the Bihar Tenancy Act, 1885, and the claims for rent for Fasli years 1356 and 1357 were barred by limitation, notwithstanding the registered instrument.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 193 and 184 of the Bihar Tenancy Act, 1885 made the Act’s provisions applicable to the suit and required dismissal of time-barred claims. Article 2(b)(i) of Schedule III supplied the special limitation period for a suit for rent in respect of forest produce; the period applied even where the claim was founded on a registered instrument. The court approved Abdulullah v. Asraf Ali, 7 C.L.J. 152, Bande Ali Fakir v. Amud Sarkar, 10 C.W.N. 415, and Mackenzie v. Haji Syed Muhammad Ali Khan, I.L.R. 19 Cal. 1.

rule.if: forest_rent_recovery_suit and lease_grants_forest_produce_rights and access_and_building_rights_are_incidental and claim_outside_special_limitation_period

predicates.forest_rent_recovery_suit: A claimant brought a suit to recover rent for rights to enjoy forest produce.
predicates.lease_grants_forest_produce_rights: The lease grants rights to cut or appropriate trees or to take fruits or flowers from trees.
predicates.access_and_building_rights_are_incidenta: Any rights to open roads or construct buildings serve only as incidents of enjoying the forest produce.
predicates.claim_outside_special_limitation_period: The rent claim was filed after the special limitation period applicable to that kind of claim had expired.

issues.definition: A suit to recover rent for leased forest-produce rights is time-barred when the lease’s access and building rights are merely incidental and the claim was filed after the applicable special limitation period.

issues.legal_issue: The statutory rate of simple interest on rent arrears overrides a contractual stipulation for a different rate when the tenancy law applies to the claim.
material_facts: The plaintiffs claimed interest on arrears of rent under the lease, which stipulated interest at one per cent in case of default.
The claim concerned rent for forest rights and was governed by the Bihar Tenancy Act, 1885.
The Act prescribed simple interest on arrears of rent at six and one-quarter per cent per annum.
issues.conclusion: Interest on the arrears was payable only at the statutory rate of simple interest, rather than at the contractual rate.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 193 and 67(1) of the Bihar Tenancy Act, 1885 applied the Act to the suit and prescribed simple interest on arrears of rent at six and one-quarter per cent per annum. Section 67(1) overrode the contractual stipulation for a different rate.

rule.if: rent_arrears_proceeding and tenancy_law_applies_to_claim and law_sets_mandatory_simple_interest_rate and contract_stipulates_a_different_interest_rate

predicates.rent_arrears_proceeding: A claimant brought a proceeding to recover arrears of rent.
predicates.tenancy_law_applies_to_claim: The governing tenancy law applies to the rent claim.
predicates.law_sets_mandatory_simple_interest_rate: The governing law prescribes a mandatory rate of simple interest on rent arrears.
predicates.contract_stipulates_a_different_interest: The lease stipulates an interest rate different from the rate prescribed by the governing law.

issues.definition: When tenancy law applies to a rent-arrears proceeding and prescribes a mandatory simple-interest rate that differs from the lease’s rate, interest is limited to the mandatory rate.
